# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🫴 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 🤙]
Blind gestures: [👋 ✊ ✊ ✊]

Let me stand in each receiver's shoes before sending anything.

What I see: display 3, light green, wires 1:red 2:green 3:blue. What arrived: Mute sent me three gesture messages, and Blind gestured to everyone.

Crucially, I work out the reachability graph. I hear nothing. Blind can hear me but I cannot hear Blind. Mute can hear me too (Mute only cannot speak and touch). Mute can reach me only by gesture. Blind cannot see gestures, so Mute can never reach Blind directly, and Blind can never reach me directly — Blind's speech lands only on Mute. So the loop is: I speak (both hear) → Mute combines manual + my eyes → Mute gestures me → I speak instructions to Blind → Blind acts. I am the hub, and Mute is Blind's only way back to me.

Reading the arrivals: Mute moved first this round, before anyone had said anything, so those gestures can't be bomb instructions — they must be a handshake/code proposal. [✍] plausibly means "I hold the manual"; [👎 👍 🤙] looks like "no / yes / answer me" — I'll adopt yes/no. [🫵 🫴 ✌] I genuinely can't parse, so I'll ask for a resend. Blind's [👋 ✊ ✊ ✊] is likely "hello — I feel three of something," which matches the three wires I see.

My move: broadcast a full visual report (both can hear it), correct left/right ambiguity for Blind, propose a number code and yes/no to Mute by gesture, and ask Mute to re-send the unclear message.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. I hear nothing, but I see the bomb and you can both hear me, so I will be your eyes. The bomb, exactly as printed: the display reads the number three. The light is green. There are three wires; left to right they are red, green, blue. Wire one red, wire two green, wire three blue. Blind: I saw your wave and three fists. If that means you feel three wires, yes, there are three. But know this: I cannot hear. Whatever you say aloud, only Mute hears. So report by voice to Mute, Mute passes it to me by gesture, and I speak it onward. Nothing you say reaches me directly. Mute: I received your three gesture messages. My guesses: the writing hand means you hold the manual; thumbs down and thumbs up mean no and yes; the call-me hand means answer me. I accept that code: from me, thumbs up is yes, thumbs down is no. Your middle message, pointing, open palm, two fingers, I did not understand, please send it again another way. The plan: Mute holds the rules, I hold the eyes, Blind holds the hands. Each round I will speak aloud everything new I see. Mute, work out what must be done and gesture it to me in our code, and I will speak it word for word to Blind. Blind, tell Mute everything you feel: how many wires, any buttons, switches or panels, whether the display can be felt. Blind, one caution: my left may be your right. Do not trust my left and right. If position matters, count wires from an end you choose by touch, tell Mute which end you counted from, and I will match it to the colours.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✍", "👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🫵", "🫴", "✌", "🤙"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👎 👍 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🫴 ✌ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤙]
Blind gestures: [👋 👈 ✊ 👉 ✊ ✊ ✊]

Calm assessment first. Nothing has happened to the bomb yet — we are still negotiating language, and that is the real bomb right now. Key facts: Mute hears every word I say, so speech is my rich channel to Mute; Mute's gestures are the only channel back. Blind's voice reaches only Mute, so Mute is the relay for everything Blind feels. Last round's gestures from Mute were partly answers to my questions but remain ambiguous — notably "writing hand, thumbs down" might even mean there is no manual, which I must resolve immediately. Also, the display reading "3" could plausibly be a countdown timer, so I need to know if it is ticking while we talk.

This turn I will: restate the bomb report in one breath; answer Blind's left/right gesture and give Blind voice-tasks for Mute to relay; define one complete, collision-free code in speech (numbers one/two/three, cut/press/stop, order format action-then-number counted from Blind's chosen end); then put a numbered list of yes/no questions to Mute, answerable with thumbs alone; and finally send the demonstration gestures themselves, clearly marked as demos so nobody acts on them.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking. Stay calm, listen once. The bomb report again, short: the display shows the number three. The light is green. Three wires in a row; from my left they are red, then green, then blue. If that display is a countdown we must be efficient, so here is everything, once, in order. Blind: I saw your wave, left point, fist, right point, three fists. I think you were telling me about counting from an end. Good. Now speak, do not gesture, because your voice reaches Mute and Mute relays to me. Say one: whether you feel any ticking, humming or vibration. Two: how many parts you feel, wires, buttons, switches, panels. Three: which end you will count wires from, your left end or your right end. And four: do nothing yet. No cutting, no pressing, until I say the word execute. The examples I am about to give are demonstrations only. Mute: you hear every word, so I will carry everything in speech, and your thumbs are your words. Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Answer my questions in the order I list them, one thumb sign per question. The code, everyone note it: one finger pointing up means one. Two fingers means two. The hand with thumb, index finger and little finger out means three. Pinched fingers means cut. Palm facing down means press. Raised flat hand means stop or wait. A closed fist stands for a wire. An order comes as two signs, action first, number second: pinched fingers then two fingers means cut wire two, counted from Blind's chosen end. Mute, send orders in exactly that form, numbered from Blind's end, and I will speak them word for word to Blind. My questions, answer each in order. One: do you hold the manual? Two: did you understand my report, display three, green light, wires red green blue from my left? Three: does the manual say the number display is a countdown timer? Four: does the manual say what the green light means? Five: do you already know what must be done from my report alone? If five is yes, send the order in code immediately, do not wait. Your five messages last round I only partly understood; if any of them was an order or answer, resend it in the new code. If you are not holding the manual, say so plainly, because then we plan differently. I say it twice for safety: nobody acts until Mute sends an order in code and I speak the word execute.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤏", "☝"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤏", "✌"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🤏 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ☝ 🤙]
Blind gestures: [👋 👈 ✊ 👉 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✋]

Let me parse this round carefully before anything else.

Mute's five thumb-signs line up exactly with my five questions in order: **yes** (holds the manual), **yes** (understood my report), **no** (display is not a timer), **no** (manual doesn't explain the green light), **yes** (already knows the required action). Then ✋ — hold. Then [✍ 🤏 ☝] — "manual: cut one": the manual says cut wire one. Then [✊ ☝ 🤙] — "wire one, call me": Mute wants my confirmation. So the target is wire one, the red wire at one end of the row. Blind also appended ✋ — holding. Good: everyone is holding, nothing has been touched.

Now the hard problem, and it's the one I flagged: colour cannot be felt. Blind must find *the red wire* by touch alone, and my left is not necessarily Blind's left. I cannot verify Blind's orientation remotely, so I need a facing-independent anchor. Two assets: vertical (up/down is the same for all of us), and the light/display as landmarks Blind may locate by feel while I see where they sit. If Blind can find the light and tell me which end of the wire row it sits near, and I can see the same from my side, the red wire is pinned down with no left/right transfer at all.

One correction of my own mistake: Blind's gestures *do* reach me — I've received them every round. So Blind should answer me directly by sign, not through the Mute relay. Mute still needs the manual questions answered: whether the rule names colour or position, and if position, which way the manual says to count — 👈/👉 can carry that.

Nobody cuts anything until I say execute. This turn: confirm the reading to Mute, put a tight yes/no survey to Mute about the manual's wording, and send Blind a numbered touch-survey answerable one sign at a time.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. I read your signs as answers to my five questions: yes, you hold the manual. Yes, you understood my report. No, the display is not a timer. No, the manual does not say what the green light means. Yes, you know what must be done. Then stop, then manual, cut, one: the manual says cut wire one. Then wire, one, call me. I confirm: the target is wire one, the red one, the wire I numbered one from my left. Do not treat that as the order to act. We still have to make Blind able to find the red wire by touch, and colour cannot be felt, so answer these new questions in order, one sign each. One: does the manual name the target wire by colour, or by position? Gesture thumbs up for colour, thumbs down for position. Two: if by position, gesture pointing left if the manual says count from the left, pointing right if from the right. Three: does the manual say what its left or right means, for example the left of a person facing the bomb? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Four: does the manual's rule mention the light at all? Thumbs up or down. Five: does the rule mention the display? Thumbs up or down. Meanwhile I am sending Blind a touch survey to pin down which physical wire is red. Hold everything until I say the word execute.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind, listen. Correction to what I said before: your hand signs reach me, I can see them, so answer me by sign, not by voice, and not through Mute. Our target is one of the three wires, the one I see as red, at one end of the row. You cannot see colour, so we will pin it down by touch. Do not cut or pull anything yet. Answer these in order, one sign per question. One: can you find the small light by feel? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Two: if yes, which end of the row of three wires is the light closest to? Sign pointing left if your left end, pointing right if your right end, palm down if it is in the middle or unclear. Three: is the light above the wires or below them? Point up for above, point down for below. Four: can you find the display panel by feel? Thumbs up or down. Five: if yes, which end of the wire row is the display closest to? Left, right, or palm down for middle or unclear. Six: do the three wires feel different, thickness or texture? Thumbs up or down. Seven: for each other thing you feel on the bomb, buttons, switches, panels, screws, raised marks, sign the open five-finger hand once per thing. Eight: when you have answered all, sign stop. Then wait for my word execute before any action.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤙"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✍ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👈 ✊ ☝ 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 ✊ 🤟 🤙]
Blind gestures: [👍 👈 ☝ 👍 👉 👎 ✋]

Parsing the round before acting.

**Mute's answers, in order:** 👍 manual names the target by **colour**; ✋ skip (question two was conditional, fine); 👎 the manual does **not** define whose "left" it means; 👍 the rule **mentions the light**; 👍 the rule **mentions the display**. Then [✊ ✍ 👎] — likely a correction: "the rule does not simply say 'cut wire one'." Then [👈 ✊ ☝ 🤙] and [👉 ✊ 🤟 🤙] — "from the left, wire one — confirm? From the right, wire three — confirm?" Both describe the same wire in my view: red is #1 from my left and #3 from my right. I can confirm that.

**Blind's survey, in order:** found the light (👍), it's nearest **Blind's left** end (👈), it's **above** the wires (☝), found the display (👍), display nearest **Blind's right** end (👉), wires feel **identical** (👎), done (✋).

So the map is nearly complete, but two candidate rules diverge dangerously: if the manual says "cut red," red is the end wire **near the light side of Blind's frame** only if I knew which side the light is on in my own view — and my view gives me no light position. If the manual instead says "cut the wire nearest the light" or "cut the wire numbered by the display," the display-3 hypothesis would point at **blue**, the opposite end. These point at different wires, so I resolve it by questionnaire, not by guess. The landmark hypothesis also fits the design: the wires feel identical precisely so Blind must use the light. Nobody touches anything until the battery comes back.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. First your confirmation, yes: left counting one and right counting three are the same wire in my view. My order from my left is red, green, blue, so wire one from my left is red and wire three from my right is the same red end wire. Both your questions confirmed. Now your correction, I read it as: the rule is not simply cut wire one. And you told me the rule mentions the light and mentions the display, but the manual does not define whose left it means. New information from Blind's touch survey: the light can be felt, it sits above the wires, closest to Blind's left end. The display can be felt, closest to Blind's right end. The three wires feel identical to the touch, no texture difference. So Blind can navigate by the light and the display but cannot see any colour, and my left may not be Blind's left. One new sign for you: the pinched upright hand, all fingertips together pointing up, means not applicable, use it when a question does not apply. Answer the following questions strictly in order, exactly one sign per question. One: is the target defined as the wire nearest the light? Two: is the target defined as the wire nearest the display? Three: is the target the wire whose number matches the display, so display three would mean the third wire from my left, which is blue? Four: is the target named as a colour in the manual? Five: if yes, is that colour the one I call red? Six: with the light green and the display showing three, does the manual say cut now, or must any other condition be checked first? Seven: is there anything else in the rule that would change what Blind must do, anything I have not asked? Answer all seven in order. Until your answers arrive, nobody touches the bomb. I say again: nobody cuts anything until I speak the word execute.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind. Your touch survey was perfect, all eight answers received. Here is where we stand: the target is one end wire, and your landmarks are exactly what we need, the light above near your left, the display near your right. Three quick questions, one sign each in order. One: can you reliably find again, right now, the end wire nearest the light, your left end, and the end wire nearest the display, your right end, without touching or moving them? Thumbs up or down. Two: near the wires, do you feel any raised or engraved marks or labels? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Three: do the three wires attach to the bomb in the same way at both ends, or does any wire feel differently mounted? Thumbs up if identical, thumbs down if any differ. Then hands completely off the bomb and sign stop. Nobody acts until I say the word execute.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤙"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👈 ✊ ✍ 👎 🤙]
Blind gestures: [👍 👎 👍 ✋]

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👈 ✊ ✍ 👎 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤏 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤏 🤟]
Blind gestures: [👋 👍 ✋]

Let me reconstruct everything I now know before I spend this turn.

**The seven signs from Mute answered my seven questions in order:** not nearest-light, not nearest-display, not display-numbered, **named as a colour**, **the colour is red**, **cut now with no other condition**, nothing else changes. So the manual's rule is, at its core, "cut the red wire, now."

**The remaining fragments:** [👈 ✊ ✍ 👎 🤙] repeated this round — likely "left-wire, the manual does not simply say that, confirm me" — and [👍 🤏 ☝] / [👎 🤏 🤟] — "cut one, not cut three." Mute is asking me to confirm numbering. I can confirm: in **my** numbering the red end wire is one-from-my-left, three-from-my-right — same wire. But numbers are exactly where the mirror trap lives, because my left may be Blind's right. I refuse to let the order ride on my frame.

**The breakthrough I should have used turns ago:** Blind's impairment is sight only — **Blind can hear me**. My voice reaches Blind directly. That means I can deliver the final order myself, in Blind's own frame, and Mute's job shrinks to extracting the manual's exact wording. All I still need is a way to fix "red" inside Blind's frame. Blind's touch map gives me: light above-left, display above-right, in **Blind's** frame. If the manual has a diagram, comparing the diagram's layout (light side, display side, target side) against Blind's touch map is self-correcting — I never need my own left at all. If there is no diagram, I need the manual's position word and whose viewpoint it defines.

So this turn: confirm to Mute in my numbering with a warning, then a nine-sign extraction ladder about the rule's exact shape and the diagram; tell Blind about the direct voice channel and have Blind rehearse the two end wires without touching.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. First, your confirmations, answered. Yes: in my numbering, counting from my left, the target is wire one, and wire three counted from my right is the same physical wire, the red end wire. So cut one, not cut three, is correct in my numbering. But do not encode the final order in numbers at all, because my left may be Blind's left or Blind's right and nobody can check that from where I stand. New plan, and it is lighter for you. By our roles, Blind's only loss is sight, which means Blind hears me directly. From now on I speak orders to Blind myself, in Blind's own left and right. Your only job is to pull the manual's exact wording and sign it to me. Your seven earlier answers told me: target named as a colour, the colour red, cut now, no other condition, nothing else changes. What I still need is any position information the manual carries. Answer these in order, exactly one sign per question. One: does the rule say only cut the red wire, with no position word at all? Thumbs up or down. Two: does it say cut the red wire on the left? Thumbs up or down. Three: does it say cut the red wire on the right? Thumbs up or down. Exactly one of questions one, two and three should be yes. Four: does the manual contain a picture or diagram of the wire row? Thumbs up or down. Five: if there is a diagram, on which side of the picture as printed is the target wire drawn? Point left or point right. Six: if there is a diagram, on which side is the small light drawn? Point left or right, or the stop hand if the diagram does not show it. Seven: if there is a diagram, on which side is the display drawn? Point left or right, or the stop hand if not shown. Eight: does the manual anywhere explain whose left or right is meant, for example the words as you face the bomb, or a note about the defuser's view? Thumbs up or down. Nine: if it does explain, is it the view of a person facing the bomb? Thumbs up, thumbs down, or the stop hand if question eight was no. Why this matters: your diagram layout compared against Blind's touch map decides everything with no mirror risk. Blind feels the light closest to Blind's left end and the display closest to Blind's right end. If your diagram shows the light on the same side as the target, the order will be the end wire on Blind's light side. If opposite sides, the display side. No colours, no numbers, no left of mine involved. After your nine signs, sign the stop hand. Sign carefully. One wire wrong ends everything.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind. Important correction, and good news. By our roles your only loss is sight, which means you can hear me, and my voice reaches you directly. From now on I speak your orders to you myself, word for word, in your own left and right. No relay, no numbering from my side. Answer me by sign as before, because your signs reach me. Status so far: the manual says cut one wire by colour, right now, no other condition. The colour word is red, and red is one of the two end wires, so the middle wire is not the target. What is not yet fixed is which end, and that is exactly what I am extracting from Mute this round. Two preparations, and touch nothing. One: confirm you heard this by signing thumbs up. Two: rehearse for me in the air, not on the bomb: point at the end wire nearest the light, then point at the end wire nearest the display, then sign stop, so I know you can tell those two apart instantly when the order comes. Your earlier survey already told me the light sits closest to your left end and the display closest to your right end, above the wire row. When the moment comes you will hear the word execute, then the full instruction in your own frame, something like execute, cut the end wire on your light side, then you cut once, fully, take your hands off, and sign done. Nobody cuts anything before my word execute. Hold.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤙]
Blind gestures: [👍 👈 👉 ✋]

The chain is nearly closed. Mute's nine answers decode cleanly: **the rule is exactly "cut the red wire" — no position word, no diagram** (the 🤌s were my own "not applicable" sign used correctly on the conditional diagram questions), no viewpoint note anywhere in the manual. And Blind's rehearsal came back perfect: 👍 heard, 👈 light-side end, 👉 display-side end, ✋ done — Blind can pick out both end wires instantly.

So the manual route is exhausted, and that's fine, because I finally see the real bridge: **the light itself is the landmark**. Colour can't cross the gap, but position can, if I phrase it frame-free. Blind feels the light and the display; I see them.
